title: Grade 4 Science — Tue, Jun 17
description: Skeletal System — Day 2 of 5: Major bones of the body
subject: science

questions.question: The skull is also called the:
questions.explanation: The skull is also called the cranium. It protects the brain and gives shape to the face.

questions.question: The spine (backbone) is made of small bones called:
questions.explanation: The spine is made of 33 small bones called vertebrae. They stack on top of each other with cartilage discs in between.

questions.question: How many vertebrae does the human spine have?
options: 33 (in childhood; some fuse to ~26 in adults)
questions.explanation: The spine has 33 vertebrae in children. Some fuse in adulthood, leaving about 26 bones. They are grouped: cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacrum, coccyx.

questions.question: The sternum is:
options: The breastbone — the flat bone in the centre of the chest
questions.explanation: The sternum (breastbone) is the flat bone in the front of the chest. The ribs attach to it. Together they form the ribcage.

questions.question: How many pairs of ribs does a human body have?
questions.explanation: Humans have 12 pairs of ribs (24 ribs total). 10 pairs attach to the sternum; the last 2 pairs are 'floating ribs' with no front attachment.

questions.question: The pelvis is:
options: The bowl-shaped set of bones at the base of the spine that supports the lower body and protects pelvic organs
questions.explanation: The pelvis (hip bone area) supports body weight, protects the bladder and reproductive organs, and connects the legs to the trunk.

questions.question: The femur is:
options: The thigh bone — the longest bone in the body
questions.explanation: The femur is the thigh bone — from the hip to the knee. It is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

questions.question: The tibia is:
options: The shin bone — the larger bone of the lower leg
questions.explanation: The tibia (shinbone) is the larger bone of the lower leg (knee to ankle). The smaller bone beside it is the fibula.

questions.question: The humerus is:
options: The upper arm bone (shoulder to elbow)
questions.explanation: The humerus is the upper arm bone, running from the shoulder to the elbow.

questions.question: The clavicle is:
options: The collar bone — connecting the shoulder blade to the sternum
questions.explanation: The clavicle (collar bone) connects the scapula (shoulder blade) to the sternum. You can feel it just below your neck.

questions.question: The scapula is the:
options: Shoulder blade — flat triangular bone on the upper back
questions.explanation: The scapula (shoulder blade) is the flat, triangular bone on the upper back. It connects the arm to the body.

questions.question: The patella is the:
options: Kneecap — the triangular bone at the front of the knee
questions.explanation: The patella (kneecap) is the small triangular bone at the front of the knee. It protects the knee joint.

questions.question: Small bones in the wrist are called:
questions.explanation: Carpals are the 8 small bones of the wrist. Tarsals are the ankle bones. Phalanges are finger/toe bones.

questions.question: Finger bones and toe bones are called:
questions.explanation: Phalanges are the bones of the fingers and toes. Each finger has 3 phalanges; the thumb has 2.

questions.question: Which bone protects the brain?
questions.explanation: The skull (cranium) is a dome of bones that completely surrounds and protects the brain.
